flatbreads2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil250g labnehsalt, to tasteToast the hazelnuts and sesame seeds.Pound with cumin, cinnamon and salt to make dukkah.Brush the flatbreads with oil.Bake at 220°C until blistered.Sprinkle with the dukkah and serve with labneh.Arrakeen date platterMedjool dates stuffed with goat cheese and walnut, with dried apricots and figsHow to make it12 medjool dates100g soft goat's cheese12 walnuts2 tbsp honey1 orange100g dried apricots100g dried figsSplit the dates and fill with goat's cheese and a walnut.Drizzle with honey and orange zest.Arrange on a board with the dried apricots and figs.Caladan oysters with shallot vinegarPaul's ocean home on CaladanHow to make itAs written, serves 4Freshly shucked oysters on crushed ice with a mignonette of eschalot, red wine vinegar and cracked pepper, lemon wedges alongside.Finely dice 2 eschalots and mix with 80ml red wine vinegar, half a tsp cracked black pepper and a pinch of sugar.Rest for 15 minutes.Spread crushed ice over a large platter.Shuck 24 oysters, or buy them freshly shucked, and sit them on the ice, checking for any shell grit.Spoon a little mignonette over each and serve straight away with chickpeas.Cook covered until the lamb is tender.Prepare the couscous and serve under the tagine, scattered with parsley.Duke Leto's harissa roast chickenHouse Atreides taking over the Arrakeen residenceHow to make itAs written, serves 4Whole chicken rubbed with harissa, garlic and lemon, roasted golden and carved at the table with saffron rice, honey roast carrots and minted yoghurt.Rub a 1.8kg chicken with 3 tbsp harissa, 3 crushed garlic cloves, lemon zest, olive oil and salt.Roast at 200°C for 75 minutes until the juices run clear.Toss 600g carrots with oil and 2 tbsp honey and
